title: STEALING THE FIRST NICE CAR
subtitle: Scan first, steal second

narration: Stealing the first beautiful car you see.
In GTA 5, any parked car was yours with one button.
Rob Nelson, who helps run Rockstar North, told IGN that the studio added layers to vehicles, so some parked cars stay out of reach until you have the right tools.
title: ROB NELSON  ·  ROCKSTAR NORTH
subtitle: LAYERS ADDED TO VEHICLES

narration: There's a phone scanner that shows a car's security level, the tool you need, whether it has an alarm or a tracker, what it would sell for, and what it costs to register.

narration: Older cars open with a slim jim.

title: tiers
subtitle: focus=3

narration: And a tracker can send police to you even when nobody saw you take the car.
title: THE TRACKER

narration: Nelson's stated goal was to make you care which car you take, instead of grabbing whatever sits at the curb.
So scan first and steal second.
title: SCAN FIRST
subtitle: STEAL SECOND

narration: Number ten.
title: A CAR YOU CAN'T KEEP
subtitle: Unregistered cars disappear

narration: Falling in love with a car you can't keep.
A stolen car you haven't registered is temporary, and previews say it disappears when you reload the game.
title: NOT REGISTERED?
subtitle: GONE WHEN YOU RELOAD

narration: Registering costs money.
In one preview, Nelson stole a car and couldn't keep it, because he hadn't done enough fence work to unlock tracker removal.
Nelson said you have to work your way up to the black market dealers who remove trackers, and trackers come in levels.
title: cards
subtitle: TRACKERS::LEVELS=Trackers come in levels|REMOVAL=Black market dealers|UNLOCK IT=Work your way up the fences

narration: One preview report even says a high level tracker won't report your location to the police while you keep your speed up, and sounds a warning when you slow down.
title: stats
subtitle: ONE REPORT::FAST=Tracker stays quiet|SLOW=Warning sounds

narration: You can park a stolen car in a garage before you register it, but Nelson told Famitsu that you start with room for just three cars.
title: garage
subtitle: YOUR FIRST GARAGE::3|Coupe|Pickup|Muscle car|Supercar

narration: Three.
title: THREE
subtitle: PARKING SPACES

narration: So when the best car on the street lands in front of you on night one, the real decision is what you're willing to push out of your garage, or whether to take it straight to a fence and cash it in.
Number nine.
title: THE WRONG WITNESS
subtitle: No witness, no stars

narration: Committing a crime in front of the wrong person.
The wanted system has been rebuilt around information.
title: THE WANTED SYSTEM
subtitle: REBUILT AROUND INFORMATION

narration: According to the previews, a crime only brings police if a witness sees it, a victim reports it, or an alarm or camera catches it.
title: cards
subtitle: HOW POLICE FIND OUT::WITNESS=Someone sees it|VICTIM=Someone reports it|ALARM OR CAMERA=A system catches it

narration: No witness, no stars.
title: NO WITNESS
subtitle: NO STARS

narration: The six star scale is back, but what matters is what sits underneath the stars.
title: stats
subtitle: THE WANTED SCALE::6=Stars are back|+=What sits under them

narration: Nelson told Famitsu that this builds on the witness idea from Red Dead Redemption 2, which means a crime nobody sees can go unreported.
Each detail the police lock in, like your appearance, your outfit, your weapon or your car, shows up as a small icon below the wanted level.
title: heat
subtitle: icons=face,outfit,weapon,vehicle

narration: So before you pull a gun in a shop, look for the camera in the corner and the person at the counter, because a quiet job and a six star manhunt can be the same job with a different witness.
Number eight.
title: SUNGLASSES WON'T SAVE YOU
subtitle: Take the description apart

narration: Believing a pair of sunglasses will save you.
Once the police have a description, previews say you have to take it apart piece by piece.
title: heat
subtitle: icons=face,outfit,weapon,vehicle off=face

narration: Changing your hair clears the hair part of the profile, but your outfit stays on file until you change your clothes.
title: heat
subtitle: icons=face,outfit,weapon,vehicle off=face,outfit

narration: The vehicle you were seen entering stays tied to you until you get rid of it.
title: heat
subtitle: icons=face,outfit,weapon,vehicle off=face,outfit,vehicle

narration: A mask can keep your face off the cameras if you wear it during the job.
And in one detail I love, splitting up with your partner during a chase can drop a star.
In GTA 5, you hid in a bush until the stars blinked.
Here, you need a plan before the crime starts.
title: HAVE A PLAN
subtitle: BEFORE THE CRIME STARTS

narration: Number seven.
title: FLEEING THREE STARS BY CAR
subtitle: Ditch it, vanish on foot

narration: Running from a three star chase in a car.
Previews say that once you hit three stars inside the city, escaping by vehicle gets hard.
The streets in Leonida are narrower, the traffic is denser, and unless your ride is very fast, the smarter move is often to ditch it and vanish on foot through the alleys.
title: cards
subtitle: WHY CARS FAIL::NARROW STREETS=Less room to weave|DENSE TRAFFIC=More to hit|ON FOOT=Vanish through the alleys

narration: Think about what that does to your first big chase.
The instinct you built over a decade, floor it and weave, may be the move that keeps the stars on.
title: FLOOR IT AND WEAVE
subtitle: MAY KEEP THE STARS ON

title: HALFWAY

narration: Number six.
title: BLOWING THE SAFE
subtitle: Fast, but the loot burns

narration: Blowing the safe because you're in a hurry.
Previews say you can rob stores, including jewelry stores and smaller banks, alone or with your partner, and every job comes with small decisions.
Blow the safe and it's fast, but part of what's inside gets destroyed.
title: cards
subtitle: THE SAFE::BLOW IT=Fast  ·  part of the loot destroyed|CRACK IT=Slower  ·  pays far more

narration: Find the combination and it takes longer, but it pays far more.
In one preview, a fence even texted the player a safe code.
One preview says the map can even show the potential take of a robbery before you commit.
title: THE POTENTIAL TAKE
subtitle: ON THE MAP BEFORE YOU COMMIT

narration: So a robbery isn't a button press.
It's a trade between speed and profit, with a camera and a witness always in the background.
title: stats
subtitle: EVERY JOB::SPEED=or|PROFIT=pick one

narration: Number five.
title: PLAYING IT SOLO
subtitle: Jason and Lucia work as a pair

narration: Playing it like a solo game.
You control Jason and Lucia, and Rockstar's previews describe jobs you can do alone or as a pair.
They also say that robbing together brings the two of them closer.
title: ROB TOGETHER
subtitle: GROW CLOSER

narration: Remember that splitting up mid chase can drop a star.
So your partner isn't a second skin on the same character.
They're an escape route, a second pair of hands, and a part of the story the game keeps track of.
title: cards
subtitle: YOUR PARTNER IS::AN ESCAPE ROUTE=Split up, drop a star|SECOND HANDS=Jobs as a pair|THE STORY=The game keeps track

narration: If you treat them like a sidekick who follows you around, you'll be using only half of what this game gives you.

narration: Thinking loot is money.
When you steal jewelry, drugs or a car, you don't get cash.
title: LOOT IS NOT MONEY

title: loop
subtitle: THE LOOP::STEAL|ESCAPE|FENCE|MONEY

narration: One report says the fence also unlocks new abilities over time, like that tracker removal.
Your first big score isn't a score until a stranger pays you for it.

subtitle: UNTIL A STRANGER PAYS YOU

title: RACING THROUGH THE STORY
subtitle: Some jobs wait for your cash

narration: Racing through the story.
In GTA 5, missions paid you.
Edge magazine reports that GTA 6 builds pauses between story missions, and sometimes Jason and Lucia need to raise cash before the next job opens.
title: EDGE MAGAZINE
subtitle: PAUSES BETWEEN STORY MISSIONS

title: cards
subtitle: CASH PAYS FOR::EQUIPMENT=Gear for the job|HUSH MONEY=Keeping people quiet|BAIL MONEY=Hopefully not

title: THE AMOUNTS
subtitle: NOT PUBLISHED
